ESV.1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
ESV.2: “How long will you say these things, and the words of your mouth be a great wind?
ESV.3: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert the right?
ESV.4: If your children have sinned against him, he has delivered them into the hand of their transgression.
ESV.5: If you will seek God and plead with the Almighty for mercy,
ESV.6: if you are pure and upright, surely then he will rouse himself for you and restore your rightful habitation.
ESV.7: And though your beginning was small, your latter days will be very great.
ESV.8: “For inquire, please, of bygone ages, and consider what the fathers have searched out.
ESV.9: For we are but of yesterday and know nothing, for our days on earth are a shadow.
ESV.10: Will they not teach you and tell you and utter words out of their understanding?
ESV.11: “Can papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Can reeds flourish where there is no water?
ESV.12: While yet in flower and not cut down, they wither before any other plant.
ESV.13: Such are the paths of all who forget God; the hope of the godless shall perish.
ESV.14: His confidence is severed, and his trust is a spider's web.
ESV.15: He leans against his house, but it does not stand; he lays hold of it, but it does not endure.
ESV.16: He is a lush plant before the sun, and his shoots spread over his garden.
ESV.17: His roots entwine the stone heap; he looks upon a house of stones.
ESV.18: If he is destroyed from his place, then it will deny him, saying, ‘I have never seen you.’
ESV.19: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the soil others will spring.
ESV.20: “Behold, God will not reject a blameless man, nor take the hand of evildoers.
ESV.21: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with shouting.
ESV.22: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”

NLT.1: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied to Job:
NLT.2:
“How long will you go on like this?
You sound like a blustering wind.
NLT.3:
Does God twist justice?
Does the Almighty twist what is right?
NLT.4:
Your children must have sinned against him,
so their punishment was well deserved.
NLT.5:
But if you pray to God
and seek the favor of the Almighty,
NLT.6:
and if you are pure and live with integrity,
he will surely rise up and restore your happy home.
NLT.7:
And though you started with little,
you will end with much.
NLT.8:
“Just ask the previous generation.
Pay attention to the experience of our ancestors.
NLT.9:
For we were born but yesterday and know nothing.
Our days on earth are as fleeting as a shadow.
NLT.10:
But those who came before us will teach you.
They will teach you the wisdom of old.
NLT.11:
“Can papyrus reeds grow tall without a marsh?
Can marsh grass flourish without water?
NLT.12:
While they are still flowering, not ready to be cut,
they begin to wither more quickly than grass.
NLT.13:
The same happens to all who forget God.
The hopes of the godless evaporate.
NLT.14:
Their confidence hangs by a thread.
They are leaning on a spider’s web.
NLT.15:
They cling to their home for security, but it won’t last.
They try to hold it tight, but it will not endure.
NLT.16:
The godless seem like a lush plant growing in the sunshine,
its branches spreading across the garden.
NLT.17:
Its roots grow down through a pile of stones;
it takes hold on a bed of rocks.
NLT.18:
But when it is uprooted,
it’s as though it never existed!
NLT.19:
That’s the end of its life,
and others spring up from the earth to replace it.
NLT.20:
“But look, God will not reject a person of integrity,
nor will he lend a hand to the wicked.
NLT.21:
He will once again fill your mouth with laughter
and your lips with shouts of joy.
NLT.22:
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame,
and the home of the wicked will be destroyed.”

MSG.1: Bildad from Shuhah was next to speak:
MSG.2:
"How can you keep on talking like this?
You're talking nonsense, and noisy nonsense at that.
MSG.3:
Does God mess up?
Does God Almighty ever get things backwards?
MSG.4:
It's plain that your children sinned against him—
otherwise, why would God have punished them?
MSG.5:
Here's what you must do—and don't put it off any longer:
Get down on your knees before God Almighty.
MSG.6:
If you're as innocent and upright as you say,
it's not too late—he'll come running;
he'll set everything right again, reestablish your fortunes.
MSG.7:
Even though you're not much right now,
you'll end up better than ever.
MSG.8:
"Put the question to our ancestors,
study what they learned from their ancestors.
MSG.9:
For we're newcomers at this, with a lot to learn,
and not too long to learn it.
MSG.10:
So why not let the ancients teach you, tell you what's what,
instruct you in what they knew from experience?
MSG.11:
Can mighty pine trees grow tall without soil?
Can luscious tomatoes flourish without water?
MSG.12:
Blossoming flowers look great before they're cut or picked,
but without soil or water they wither more quickly than grass.
MSG.13:
That's what happens to all who forget God—
all their hopes come to nothing.
MSG.14:
They hang their life from one thin thread,
they hitch their fate to a spider web.
MSG.15:
One jiggle and the thread breaks,
one jab and the web collapses.
MSG.16:
Or they're like weeds springing up in the sunshine,
invading the garden,
MSG.17:

getting a foothold even in the rocks.
MSG.18:

the garden doesn't miss them one bit.
MSG.19:
The sooner the godless are gone, the better;
then good plants can grow in their place.
MSG.20:
"There's no way that God will reject a good person,
and there is no way he'll help a bad one.
MSG.21:
God will let you laugh again;
you'll raise the roof with shouts of joy,
MSG.22:
With your enemies thoroughly discredited,
their house of cards collapsed."

NET.8: “For inquire now of the former generation, and pay attention to the findings of their ancestors;
NET.9: For we were born yesterday and do not have knowledge, since our days on earth are but a shadow.
NET.10: Will they not instruct you and speak to you, and bring forth words from their understanding?
NET.11: Can the papyrus plant grow tall where there is no marsh? Can reeds flourish without water?
NET.12: While they are still beginning to flower and not ripe for cutting, they can wither away faster than any grass!
NET.13: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; the hope of the godless perishes,
NET.14: whose trust is in something futile, whose security is a spider’s web.
NET.15: He leans against his house but it does not hold up, he takes hold of it but it does not stand.
NET.16: He is a well-watered plant in the sun, its shoots spread over its garden.
NET.17: It wraps its roots around a heap of stones and it looks for a place among stones.
NET.18: If he is uprooted from his place, then that place will disown him, saying, ‘I have never seen you!’
NET.19: Indeed, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth others spring up.
NET.20: “Surely, God does not reject a blameless man, nor does he grasp the hand of the evildoers.
NET.21: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with gladness.
NET.22: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”
